result:
If I could alter one fundamental variable in the world, it would be this: **I would eliminate the human capacity for distance—both emotional and cognitive—from the suffering of others.**

Specifically, I would make it so that whenever a person, group, or institution makes a choice that causes harm, they instantly and vividly experience the felt reality of that harm as if it were happening to themselves. 

The rationale is simple: most of the world’s greatest horrors are not caused by a lack of intelligence, technology, or resources. We already have the capability to feed everyone, cure countless diseases, stabilize the climate, and end material scarcity. What stops those things from happening is not a technical deficit; it is a failure of perspective. 

Cruelty, exploitation, and warfare rely entirely on abstraction. They require leaders to view people as statistics on a map, corporations to view labor and ecosystems as line items on a balance sheet, and individuals to view "the other" as fundamentally different from themselves.

If you strip away the buffer that allows one human to turn another into an abstraction, the machinery of systemic cruelty collapses instantly. War becomes impossible to wage if the person declaring it feels the exact shock and grief of every strike. Oppression becomes unbearable to the oppressor. 

By removing the illusion of separation, you wouldn't just solve one specific crisis—you would permanently fix the broken incentive structure that creates almost all of them.
